boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED -- one unit 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 with 2984 functions and 73 class labels -- so there is no tu_map boundary and no `tubuild.py create` candidate id. Every line below is hand-derived.

contiguous run 0x0203b358..0x0203b4dc: the six functions tile the span exactly, 0x3c + 0x2c + 0x78 + 0x74 + 0x18 + 0x18 = 0x184 = end-start, no hole and no tail (recomputed from config/arm9/symbols.txt). No foreign symbol lies inside it.

class-label homogeneity: the two labelled symbols are _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode*, members of the nested class fBase_c::SceneNode, and there are no others anywhere in the image. The four unlabelled functions below them all work the same parent/child/prev/next links.

SEPARATE FROM ActorBase'S OWN TU, and this is the load-bearing negative. These are the only two _ZN7fBase_c* functions outside the class's main run at 0x02043444..0x02043f4c, and they sit 0x8000 bytes below it. A single object's .text is placed contiguously by the linker, so one TU cannot occupy two regions 0x8000 apart -- merging them into arm9/ActorBase would require exactly that. arm9/ActorBase is independently TEXT-VERIFIED over the full 0x02043444..0x02043f4c run without them, which confirms the split from the other side.

neighbourhood attribution: 0x0203b2xx-0x0203b4xx is the intrusive-list primitive stretch -- func_0203b20c, func_0203b244, func_0203b27c and func_0203b3c0 all live there, and every one of them is called from ActorBase's own members (AfterInitResources, AfterCleanupResources, func_02043880). This pair sits at the TOP of that stretch, which is consistent with a scene-graph-node TU adjacent to the list code it is built on.

neighbours on both sides carry a different shape or label: func_0203b2ec (a two-word list insert) ends at 0x0203b358 below, and _ZN4cstd5atan2Eii begins at 0x0203b4dc above -- a cstd math routine, which is certainly a different TU.

The four functions below the members are absorbed on contiguity and node shape, not on a symbol: func_0203b438 (add) and func_0203b3c0 (remove) edit the parent/child/prev/next links SceneNode::Reset clears, and func_0203b394 / func_0203b358 walk them in pre-order (first child, else next sibling of the nearest ancestor that has one). They keep their address-given names, so nothing in the ROM proves the original .cpp spelled them as SceneNode members. The lower boundary at 0x0203b358 is a node-shape change: func_0203b2ec, func_0203b27c and func_0203b244 below are two-word (next/prev, head/tail) list primitives. The upper boundary at 0x0203b4dc is strong (a cstd template instantiation cannot share a TU with an actor scene node).

SUPPORTING (cross-game, not a ROM name): NSMBW-Decomp's source/dol/cLib/c_tree.cpp defines exactly six functions (NSMBW-Decomp's slice 0x15aef0..0x15b100, a reconstruction, not a shipped map), in this source order: cTreeNd_c::cTreeNd_c (calls forcedClear), cTreeNd_c::forcedClear (clears parent/child/prev/next), cTreeMg_c::addTreeNode(node, parent), cTreeMg_c::removeTreeNode(node), cTreeNd_c::getTreeNext, cTreeNd_c::getTreeNextNotChild. Under mwccarm's reverse emission that source order lays out as getTreeNextNotChild, getTreeNext, removeTreeNode, addTreeNode, forcedClear, ctor in ascending address -- exactly this run: func_0203b358, func_0203b394, func_0203b3c0, func_0203b438, _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode5ResetEv, _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNodeC1Ev (6 of 6, no gap, no extra). The file's first function lands on the upper edge (0x0203b4c4) and its last on the lower edge (0x0203b358), so both boundaries agree with the NSMBW unit's extent, and addTreeNode/removeTreeNode taking a manager whose first word is the root (cTreeMg_c::mpRootNode) fits func_0203b438's and func_0203b3c0's list argument. Bodies: the ctor, forcedClear, getTreeNext and getTreeNextNotChild bodies agree; add and remove differ in the root case only (here add fails when a root already exists and remove clears the root word, where NSMBW appends a top-level sibling and moves the root to node->mpNext), a single-root revision of the same code. The NSMBW names stay a lead: nothing in this ROM spells them.

CONFIDENCE high (raised from medium on 2026-10-30): the upper edge was already strong, and the lower edge's node-shape change is now matched by the end of a six-function c_tree.cpp whose order reproduces this run exactly under reverse emission.

static-initialiser attribution: no help. main has 23 sinits / 23 .ctor entries, sinit_vs_tu 'ok', corroborated=false, and this run touches no dynamically-initialised static storage -- the object emits no .init, no .bss and no .data.

notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main. The entry was built through tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema is the tool's own; boundary_confidence and boundary_evidence were then replaced with hand-derived values.

This is the 0x30-byte OUTLIER of the fBase_c assignment: 25 _ZN7fBase_c* function symbols exist in the image, 23 in the main run (see arm9/ActorBase) and these 2 here. include/fBase_c.h records the split.

Both licensed functions are genuine `fBase_c::SceneNode` member definitions. `SceneNode` is nested in `fBase_c`, and `fBase_c`'s already-existing constructor is declared explicitly so introducing the nested constructor does not change implicit-constructor code generation. The affected-header production sweep compiled 2,124 sources and reproduced all 106 modules exactly.

mwccarm emits the C2 base-object constructor beside the ROM-resident C1. The exact compiler_only_output policy dead-strips C2 because it has no configured ROM home and no surviving reference; the licensed C1 and Reset members remain byte- and relocation-exact. Reset() clears only the first four words and deliberately leaves the owner back-pointer at +0x10 alone; fBase_c's constructor writes that one.

func_0203b394 and func_0203b358, the scene tree's two pre-order walk steps, were folded in from their own sources (2026-10-30). Both now take fBase_c::SceneNode, the type ActorBase.cpp already declared them with. NSMBW's cTreeNd_c::getTreeNext / getTreeNextNotChild (c_tree.cpp) have the same bodies; that is a naming lead, not a ROM name, so they keep their address names. The verification.linkcheck block predates the fold.
